correctness.rationale: Every normalization and quantifier was checked: uniform pairings of 2n cyclic endpoints for n≥2, span=min of the two internal endpoint counts, n^{3/2} scaling. Edge inclusion probabilities yield S1,S2 and the span variance; conditioning on one chord yields the mixed covariance. Crossing variance is Flajolet–Noy's established formula. IID endpoints produce the matching law; total span is bounded below by the short-arc occupancy U-statistic with exact expected approximation gap n(n−1)/(2(2n−1))=O(n). The bounded first-order Hoeffding projections are 2q−1/2 and 2q(1−q)−1/3, q uniform (0,1/2), with exact covariance 1/12,1/24,1/45 and an O(n²) degenerate remainder. Bivariate iid CLT and Markov comparison prove the infinite limit, not merely finite simulation. An independent exact-rational script checked all five finite moments for n=2..7 (146,598 matchings), polynomial projection integrals, determinant 1/8640 and regression residual variance 1/720. No unsupported independence, exact finite Gaussianity, or rate of convergence is asserted.

value.rationale: Total discrete shorter-arc span is the most direct global circular-length measure on labeled chord diagrams, while number of crossings is the intersection-graph edge count. Their global dependence is not determined by single-chord conditional degree distributions or one-variable crossing moments. The new bivariate law identifies exact asymptotic correlation sqrt(15)/4 and explains 15/16 of crossing fluctuation variance from chord spans, with an irreducible Gaussian residual of variance 1/720. This structural calibration has a concrete statistical interpretation and is not a mere reparameterization, trivial estimate, or unsupported tiny finite improvement.
